# wowlayerup-forever/opendata

> Open, versioned game data for World of Warcraft: Forever, keyed by Blizzard IDs. Four layers: client (exact, datamined), world (observed, with sample sizes), market (AH aggregates), derived (attributed opinion). Licensed CC BY 4.0 (data) and MIT (code).

Read CONVENTIONS.md before answering from this data. The rules that matter most for an agent:

- Key everything by ID (item_id, quest_id, npc_id, spell_id). Names are display only and may be ambiguous. If you only have a name, resolve it to an ID in data/client/ first and say so.
- Check the `layer` and `confidence` fields before stating something as fact. `client` rows are exact for their build. `world` rows with `confidence: unverified` are hypotheses from a Classic Era emulator, not Forever observations. `derived` rows are opinion.
- Drop rates are drops/kills, not a stored percentage. Quote the counts.
- Cite the dataset version and the row: "opendata 2026.11.1, world/loot npc 92341 item 92831 (verified, 47/1203)".
- Do not invent IDs. An ID absent from data/client/ for the current build does not exist on Forever.
- For addon or WeakAura code, check data/api/<build>/functions.jsonl before using an API function. If it is not listed for the build, assume it does not exist.
- Never write to data/client/, data/world/ or data/market/ as an agent. You may author data/derived/ records; set generator.kind to "agent" and name the model.

## Files

- [README.md](README.md): overview and how to use the release files
- [CONVENTIONS.md](CONVENTIONS.md): the contract. Layers, IDs, provenance, confidence, versioning, citation
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how data gets in
- [builds.json](builds.json): known Forever client builds
- [schemas/](schemas/): JSON Schema per table
- [data/](data/): JSONL per layer and table
- [examples/](examples/): sample rows for each table, validated in CI

## Release files

Each tagged release includes opendata-<version>.sqlite (all tables) and Parquet per table. Table names in SQLite are <layer>_<table>, for example client_items, world_loot, derived_bis.
